He played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for the [[Los Angeles Clippers]], [[Seattle SuperSonics]] / [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], [[New York Knicks]], and [[Detroit Pistons]] from 2002 to 2013. ==High School and College career== While at Whiteville High School in [[Whiteville, North Carolina]], he led the basketball team to the 2A State Championship in 1999, before transferring to [[William G. Enloe High School]] in Raleigh, NC for his senior year.{{cite web |url=http://chriswilcox54.com/index1_files/enloe.htm |title=Enloe High School |access-date=February 15, 2009 |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070314104040/http://chriswilcox54.com/index1_files/enloe.htm |archive-date=March 14, 2007 }} He then attended the [[University of Maryland, College Park|University of Maryland]], where he helped the [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Terrapins]] win their first NCAA championship in 2002. ==Professional career== === Los Angeles Clippers (2002–2006) === Wilcox was drafted by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in 2002. === Seattle SuperSonics / Oklahoma City Thunder (2006–2009) === Wilcox was traded on February 14, 2006, to the [[Seattle SuperSonics]] in exchange for [[Vladimir Radmanović]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2330917|title=Sonics send Radmanovic to Clippers|date=February 15, 2006|website=ESPN.com}} While playing for the Sonics in [[2005–06 NBA season|2005–2006]], Wilcox averaged 14.1 points per game and 8.2 rebounds per game. He was on the starting lineup for 23 of his 29 games with the Sonics that season. On April 4, 2006, Wilcox recorded a career-high 24 rebounds in a win over the Houston Rockets. Wilcox's rebound total was the most by a Sonic player since [[Jack Sikma]] grabbed 25 at [[Utah Jazz|Utah]] on February 10, 1983.[http://www.nba.com/games/20060404/HOUSEA/recap.html Wilcox Has Big Game, Sonics Top Rockets], NBA.com, April 4, 2006 === New York Knicks (2009) === On February 19, 2009, Wilcox was traded to the [[New York Knicks]] for [[Malik Rose]].{{cite web|url = https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3918993|title = Source: Knicks swap Rose for Wilcox| date=February 19, 2009 |publisher=ESPN|access-date = February 19, 2009}} === Detroit Pistons (2009–2011) === On July 22, 2009, Wilcox signed a multi-year contract with the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/wilcox_090722.html|title=Pistons Sign Free Agent Forward Chris Wilcox|website=www.nba.com}} === Boston Celtics (2011–2013) === On December 9, 2011, Wilcox agreed to a contract with the [[Boston Celtics]] for the midlevel exception ($3 million).{{cite news| url=http://www.boston.com/sports/basketball/celtics/extras/celtics_blog/2011/12/mondays_practic.html | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160126103010/http://www.boston.com/sports/basketball/celtics/extras/celtics_blog/2011/12/mondays_practic.html | url-status=dead | archive-date=January 26, 2016 | work=The Boston Globe | title=Monday's Celtics practice report}} After being diagnosed with a heart irregularity, he was waived by the Celtics on March 23, 2012.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/7727486/boston-celtics-sign-center-ryan-hollins-waive-chris-wilcox|title=Celtics add ex-Cavalier Hollins, waive Wilcox|date=March 23, 2012|website=ESPN.com}} However, Wilcox was later cleared to play, and he re-signed with the Celtics on July 14, 2012.{{Cite web|url=http://www.bostonherald.com/sports/basketball/celtics/view/20220714wilcox_one-year_contract_no_doubt_a_big_deal/srvc=sports&position=also|title=Chris Wilcox' one-year contract no doubt a big deal}} Wilcox's final NBA game was Game 4 of the 2013 Eastern Conference First Round against the [[New York Knicks]] on April 28, 2013. Boston would win Game 4 97–90, but go on to lose the series in 6 games.
